```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                       fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# reserves blank work space (no ruled lines); pair with fig.height
blank_space <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
}

# fill-in table drawn with base graphics so row height is controllable;
# body = list of rows, each a list/vector of cell strings ("" = blank)
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5, cex = 0.95) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
    text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, h_total - header_height / 2, headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  }
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      if (!identical(body[[i]][[j]], "")) {
        text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, y - row_height / 2, body[[i]][[j]], cex = cex)
      }
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}

# keeps a prompt and its answer space on one PDF page: place `r nq(...)` on its
# own line just above the prompt. Emits nothing in non-LaTeX output. lines =
# lines of prompt text, rows = rows of blank space below it (0.3 in each),
# extra = any other height (in inches), e.g. a figure or table
nq <- function(lines, rows = 0, extra = 0) {
  if (!knitr::is_latex_output()) return("")
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf("\n\\needspace{%.2fin}\n", 0.23 * lines + 0.15 + 0.3 * rows + extra))
}

seedlings <- read.csv("../data/PinyonSeedlings.csv")
fit_check <- lm(growth ~ plot + moisture, data = seedlings)
f2 <- function(v) formatC(round(v, 2) + 0, format = "f", digits = 2)
```

## The scenario

A restoration crew planted pinyon pine seedlings in three burned plots
(A, B, and C) in a Great Basin woodland. A year later you measured each
seedling's height growth (cm) and the soil moisture (%) next to it: 8
seedlings per plot, 24 in all. The six seedlings below are the first
three in plots A and B.

```{r six-seedlings}
six <- seedlings[c(1:3, 9:11), c("plot", "seedling", "moisture")]
knitr::kable(six, row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("Plot", "Seedling", "Soil moisture (%)"),
             align = "ccc")
```

The crew's model is an ANCOVA: each plot has its own intercept, and all
plots share one slope for soil moisture,

$$\text{growth}_i \sim \text{Normal}(\mu_i, \sigma^2), \qquad
\mu_i = \beta_0 + \beta_B\,[\text{plot B}]_i + \beta_m\,\text{moisture}_i$$

where $[\text{plot B}]_i$ is 1 for a plot-B seedling and 0 otherwise.
(For the six seedlings there are only two plots.)

**How much does soil moisture matter, and what does this model assume
about seedlings that grow side by side in the same plot?**

Please keep laptops closed until the banner in Part 2. Part 1 and the
group check-in are pen and paper.

`r nq(4, 9)`

**1d.** Suppose the six growth values are independent with
$\sigma = 0.5$ cm. Write the covariance matrix $V$, its inverse, and
its determinant. Then suppose plot B is more variable, with
$\sigma_B = 1$ cm (plot A stays at 0.5). Write the new $V$, and write
the quadratic form $\mathbf{r}^TV^{-1}\mathbf{r}$ for a residual vector

residual count compared with a plot-A residual of the same size?


`r nq(8, 12)`

**1e.** Two seedlings grow side by side in the same plot, and their
residuals have correlation 0.5 (each with variance 1):

$$V = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0.5 \\ 0.5 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Find $|V|$ and $V^{-1}$. Compute $\mathbf{r}^TV^{-1}\mathbf{r}$ for
$\mathbf{r} = (1, 1)^T$ and for $\mathbf{r} = (1, -1)^T$, and compare
both with independence ($V = I$). Which pattern of residuals is more
surprising when the seedlings are correlated, and why does that make
sense?

## Group discussion and revision (~15 min)

Close laptops. Here is a different covariance matrix someone proposed
for the six seedlings in the table (rows and columns in the same
order: A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3):

$$V = \begin{pmatrix}
1 & 0.6 & 0.6 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
0.6 & 1 & 0.6 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
0.6 & 0.6 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0.6 & 0.6 \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0.6 & 1 & 0.6 \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0.6 & 0.6 & 1
\end{pmatrix}$$

With your group, say what this $V$ claims about the seedlings, and what
could make the 0.6s biologically reasonable. Should the crew treat its
24 seedlings as 24 independent replicates when reporting the effect of
plot? Record your answer, any changes you made to earlier answers, new
